temaNombre: Spanish Spelling: LL/Y, R/RR and C/Z
title: Spelling Masters
summary: Practise Spanish ll/y, r/rr and c/z spellings in everyday words and texts.
keyIdeas: The endings -illo and -illa use ll. Forms such as «leyó» and «cayó» use y even though their infinitives do not.
The strong r sound uses rr between vowels, but a single r at the start of a word or after l, n or s in these examples.
Examples include c in «cena/cine» and z in «zapato/zorro/zumo». Exceptions include «zeta». Nouns ending in -z usually form plurals in -ces.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas de producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Aisha prepares for art class. Which pair correctly completes «Tengo un ___ afilado y tres ___ de colores»? ✏️
activities.explanation: «Lápiz» becomes «lápices», changing z to c before e. Some other words use z before e, such as «zeta».
activities.hint: Remember how the singular ending changes in the plural.

activities.prompt: After l, n and s, the strong r sound must be written rr, as in «alrrededor» and «enrredo».
activities.explanation: False. These examples use one r: «alrededor», «enredo», «sonrisa» and «Israel».

activities.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt Spanish word.
activities.explanation: The diminutive suffixes -illo and -illa use ll.
activities.sentence: Lucía guardó las llaves de la bicicleta en el ___ delantero de su mochila.

activities.prompt: Sort these words by whether their strong r sound uses r or rr.
activities.explanation: The strong sound uses r in «ratón», «alrededor» and «sonrisa». Between vowels, «carrera», «pelirrojo» and «pararrayos» use rr.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish singular noun with its correct plural.
activities.explanation: In these words, the singular -z changes to plural -ces.

activities.prompt: Hugo writes four sentences in his trip diary. Which has a Spanish spelling error?
activities.explanation: The verb «caer» gives «cayó», meaning fell. «Calló» comes from «callar», meaning became silent.
options: Adrián organizó un partido de baloncesto en el recreo.
Ayer el payaso se calló de la silla durante la función.
Mi tío Enrique coció unas ricas verduras en la cazuela.
El perro corrió veloz por la orilla del río.

activities.prompt: Complete with the correctly spelt past form of «leer».
activities.explanation: The form is «leyó», with y. It is stressed on the last syllable and ends in a vowel, so it also needs an accent mark.
activities.sentence: Ayer Martina ___ un cómic enterito antes de merendar.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish trip text and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Notice the spellings while understanding the story.
activities.title: Aventura en el jardín botánico
activities.text:
El pasado martes, el grupo de quinto visitó el jardín botánico con su maestra Nerea. Nada más cruzar la cancela de hierro, un suave olor a azahar y tierra mojada llenó el ambiente. Omar observó con atención un cartel de madera que señalaba el sendero de los helechos. Mientras caminaban en fila, un pájaro de plumaje brillante y pico rojizo se posó en una rama cercana.

Lucía sacó su libreta para anotar los detalles: descubrieron un estanque con diminutos peces de colores y una zona llena de calabacines y cebollas gigantes. De repente, una ráfaga de viento movió las hojas secas del suelo y todos oyeron un crujido misterioso. Al acercarse con cuidado entre los matorrales, descubrieron a un erizo enrollado junto a un castaño centenario. El jardinero Enrique les explicó que el animalillo buscaba refugio antes de que cayera la lluvia de la tarde.

questions.prompt: What animal did they discover among the bushes?
questions.explanation: The text describes a curled-up hedgehog among the bushes.
options: A bird with a reddish beak.

questions.prompt: Why did Enrique think the hedgehog was seeking shelter?
questions.explanation: Enrique suggests it was sheltering before rain. This is his explanation in the story; the observation does not prove that the animal predicted the weather.
options: Because it was hungry and wanted chestnuts.
Because rain or a storm was approaching.
Because it was escaping the pupils' noise.

questions.prompt: Which spelling statement about «peces», «oyeron», «Enrique» and «animalillo» is correct?
questions.explanation: «Peces» is the plural of «pez», changing z to c. «Oyeron» is a form of «oír» with y. «Enrique» has a strong r after n.
options: «Peces» uses c in the plural of «pez»; «oyeron» is a form of «oír» written with y.
«Enrique» has one r because its sound is weak.
«Animalillo» uses ll because it starts with a vowel.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish words by whether they use ll or y.
activities.explanation: «Folleto», «mantequilla» and «castillo» use ll. «Proyectil», «bueyes» and «desayuno» use y. Starting with fo- does not automatically require ll: compare «foto».

activities.prompt: Which Spanish compound word is spelt correctly? 🧠
activities.explanation: When «rayos» follows «para», its initial strong r falls between vowels and is doubled: «pararrayos».
activities.hint: A strong r between vowels is written rr.
